description: The plot illustrates how accuracy varies as a function of object population frequency for two series labeled “Initial Accuracy” and “Final Accuracy.” The x-axis is labeled “o_pop frequency (x10^4)” and uses a linear scale with discrete tick marks at 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15, 17, and 19 (values shown in units of ×10^4). The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy,” spans approximately 0.0 to 1.0 on a linear scale, and shows regularly spaced tick labels at about 0.2 intervals. The “Initial Accuracy” series is drawn as a green solid line with square markers and vertical error bars with caps; it starts near 0.34 at x=1, rises to about 0.49 at x=5, drops to around 0.29 at x=7, increases to about 0.53 at x=13, then is around 0.41 at x=15, about 0.36 at x=17, and ends near 0.41 at x=19. The “Final Accuracy” series is drawn as a blue dashed line with circular markers and vertical error bars with caps; it begins near 0.65 at x=1, is around 0.80 at x=3 and 0.86 at x=5, dips to about 0.72 at x=7, peaks near 0.92 at x=9, drops to about 0.70 at x=11 and about 0.68 at x=13, rises to around 0.90 at x=15, is about 0.81 at x=17, and ends near 0.90 at x=19.
